title: Recovery of a flatly extended primary ideal on its radical fibre
statement:
Let $f:R\to S$ be a flat homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $q\subset R$ be a primary ideal: $q\ne R$ and $ab\in q$, $a\notin q$ imply $b^h\in q$ for some $h\ge1$. Put $\mathfrak p=\sqrt q=\{a\in R:a^h\in q\text{ for some }h\ge1\}$. For each prime $\mathfrak Q\subset S$ with $f^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak p$, let $S_{\mathfrak Q}$ be its prime localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $\lambda_{\mathfrak Q}:S\to S_{\mathfrak Q}$ the canonical map. For any ideal $H\subseteq S$, write $HS_{\mathfrak Q}$ for its extension. Then
$$qS=\bigcap_{\mathfrak Q\cap R=\mathfrak p}\lambda_{\mathfrak Q}^{-1}(qS_{\mathfrak Q}).$$
The empty intersection means $S$. Neither faithful flatness nor reducedness of $S/\mathfrak pS$ is required.

proof.text: Tensor this injection with the flat $R$-module $S$, using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring](1), $(R/q)\otimes_RS\cong S/qS$, via $\bar r\otimes s\mapsto f(r)s\bmod I$. On these generators, the tensor of multiplication by $a$ becomes multiplication by $f(a)$. Consequently $f(a)$ acts injectively on $M$ for every $a\notin\mathfrak p$.

proof.text: Apply the equivalent annihilator criterion in [lem-weil-pbc-module-injects-localizations-associated-primes] to the $S$-module $M$; $S$ is Noetherian by hypothesis. Step 4 supplies its required annihilator outside every associated prime. Hence $\bar x=0$, so $x\in I=qS$. This proves equality, including an empty fibre: in that case Step 3 implies there are no associated primes and the same criterion forces $M=0$, hence $qS=S$.
